Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-transcribe-long-0099", "row_sha256": "5f799639a3e10880725d6ff098074dee936fff1622322271ba52aa465e2a9dc5", "mode": "/transcribe", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Remove true hesitation and accidental restarts. Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "
okay i need to leave a clear handoff for the people covering the north quay shared folder this week because the sync client has been acting differently on the office laptop and the two machines in the reading room the folder is called north quay oral history and it holds interview audio scans and the release forms the current client version is 4.8.2 on all three machines i checked the version screen yesterday afternoon and the laptop is running windows 11 while the reading room machines are both on macos 14.4 the network is the same staff network but the laptop sometimes moves to the guest wifi when it wakes up so that may explain why its status is not always matching the other two

please check the setting called
sync.limit_uploads
in the shared folder profile on the laptop and tell me what value is there before changing anything i want the upload limit set to 12 megabits per second during the daytime transfer window from 9 am to 4 pm but only if the setting is currently higher than 12 if it is already 12 or lower leave it alone and note the value instead the 12 is megabits per second not megabytes per second and it is a speed limit not a file size limit i saw two people mix those up last month don't apply that limit to downloads and don't change the global profile because the collections team uses it for a different project

i checked the queue at 10 20 this morning and there were 38 items waiting 26 were audio files and 12 were scans the largest audio file was 1.7 gigabytes and the largest scan was 84 megabytes three audio files had been paused by the client because the laptop had gone to sleep the rest were waiting behind a folder scan that started after marisol added a batch of release forms at 9 55 i think the pause happened around 10 05 but the client only shows the last connection time as 10 08 so please treat that time as approximate not as an exact pause time the folder scan can take 15 to 20 minutes when those forms arrive together

for the handoff, number one check that all three devices show the same folder name and the same client version before you resume anything number two look at the laptop network indicator and confirm it says staff wifi rather than guest wifi number three inspect the 38 item queue again and write down the waiting count and whether any audio files still say paused number four open the per folder upload setting and compare it with 12 megabits per second during the 9 am to 4 pm window if it is higher than 12 make the requested change if it is 12 or lower do not change it number five leave the download rate as it is and leave the global profile untouched i started to say restart the client after that but no, only restart it if the queue has not changed for 20 minutes and the connection still shows staff wifi

when i spoke with marisol she said, "the forms are all in the folder, but i have not checked whether the last two scans finished uploading." she added that the paper originals are in cabinet B, drawer 4, and that the signed release forms must stay with the matching interviews the file names use the interview date first and then the speaker initials, for example 2024-05-17_LN_audio.wav the scans use the same date and initials with _release_scan at the end please don't rename files to make them sort differently because the archive index is already linked to those names the two scans she mentioned are for LN and RT and she expects to check their previews tomorrow morning

the laptop has 46 gigabytes of free disk space according to the client but the operating system showed 51 gigabytes free at 8 30 this morning that difference could be from temporary files or a delayed reading so record both numbers with their sources and don't remove anything to make more room the project has a 60 gigabyte local cache limit and i don't know if that limit includes the temporary download folder i asked support last thursday but haven't received a reply yet until we know, leave the cache setting where it is and make sure the next person knows not to treat the two free space readings as a confirmed failure

if the queue starts moving again while you're checking it, let the current transfers finish and don't pause them just to get a cleaner count if it stays unchanged for 20 minutes, first confirm the laptop is on staff wifi, then restart only the client on the laptop and check whether the three paused audio files return to waiting or active status don't restart either reading room machine unless the laptop client shows an error after that the interview team is expecting access to the scans by 2 pm, but that is their requested time, not a promise that every upload will be finished by then

before you sign off, put the observations in the north quay handoff note with the time you checked, the three device names, the client version, the queue count, the setting value, and whether you changed it include the network name and both free space readings, and say which machine each reading came from if the two scans are still unfinished, mention LN and RT without moving them into another folder the next shift begins at 1 30 pm and can continue checking the queue then leave the shared folder mounted on the reading room machines, since those are used for listening sessions, and don't sign out of the archive account on either one", "output": "Okay, I need to leave a clear handoff for the people covering the North Quay shared folder this week because the sync client has been acting differently on the office laptop and the two machines in the reading room. The folder is called North Quay Oral History, and it holds interview audio, scans, and the release forms. The current client version is 4.8.2 on all three machines. I checked the version screen yesterday afternoon, and the laptop is running Windows 11 while the reading room machines are both on macOS 14.4. The network is the same staff network, but the laptop sometimes moves to the guest Wi-Fi when it wakes up, so that may explain why its status is not always matching the other two.

Please check the setting called
sync.limit_uploads
in the shared folder profile on the laptop and tell me what value is there before changing anything. I want the upload limit set to 12 megabits per second during the daytime transfer window from 9 am to 4 pm, but only if the setting is currently higher than 12. If it is already 12 or lower, leave it alone and note the value instead. The 12 is megabits per second, not megabytes per second, and it is a speed limit, not a file size limit. I saw two people mix those up last month. Don't apply that limit to downloads, and don't change the global profile because the collections team uses it for a different project.

I checked the queue at 10:20 this morning, and there were 38 items waiting: 26 were audio files, and 12 were scans. The largest audio file was 1.7 gigabytes, and the largest scan was 84 megabytes. Three audio files had been paused by the client because the laptop had gone to sleep. The rest were waiting behind a folder scan that started after Marisol added a batch of release forms at 9:55. I think the pause happened around 10:05, but the client only shows the last connection time as 10:08, so please treat that time as approximate, not as an exact pause time. The folder scan can take 15 to 20 minutes when those forms arrive together.

For the handoff:
1. Check that all three devices show the same folder name and the same client version before you resume anything.
2. Look at the laptop network indicator and confirm it says staff Wi-Fi rather than guest Wi-Fi.
3. Inspect the 38-item queue again and write down the waiting count and whether any audio files still say paused.
4. Open the per-folder upload setting and compare it with 12 megabits per second during the 9 am to 4 pm window. If it is higher than 12, make the requested change. If it is 12 or lower, do not change it.
5. Leave the download rate as it is and leave the global profile untouched.

I started to say restart the client after that, but no, only restart it if the queue has not changed for 20 minutes and the connection still shows staff Wi-Fi.

When I spoke with Marisol, she said, “The forms are all in the folder, but I have not checked whether the last two scans finished uploading.” She added that the paper originals are in cabinet B, drawer 4, and that the signed release forms must stay with the matching interviews. The file names use the interview date first and then the speaker initials, for example, 2024-05-17_LN_audio.wav. The scans use the same date and initials with _release_scan at the end. Please don't rename files to make them sort differently because the archive index is already linked to those names. The two scans she mentioned are for LN and RT, and she expects to check their previews tomorrow morning.

The laptop has 46 gigabytes of free disk space according to the client, but the operating system showed 51 gigabytes free at 8:30 this morning. That difference could be from temporary files or a delayed reading, so record both numbers with their sources and don't remove anything to make more room. The project has a 60-gigabyte local cache limit, and I don't know if that limit includes the temporary download folder. I asked support last Thursday but haven't received a reply yet. Until we know, leave the cache setting where it is and make sure the next person knows not to treat the two free-space readings as a confirmed failure.

If the queue starts moving again while you're checking it, let the current transfers finish and don't pause them just to get a cleaner count. If it stays unchanged for 20 minutes, first confirm the laptop is on staff Wi-Fi, then restart only the client on the laptop and check whether the three paused audio files return to waiting or active status. Don't restart either reading room machine unless the laptop client shows an error after that. The interview team is expecting access to the scans by 2 pm, but that is their requested time, not a promise that every upload will be finished by then.

Before you sign off, put the observations in the North Quay handoff note with the time you checked, the three device names, the client version, the queue count, the setting value, and whether you changed it. Include the network name and both free-space readings, and say which machine each reading came from. If the two scans are still unfinished, mention LN and RT without moving them into another folder. The next shift begins at 1:30 pm and can continue checking the queue then. Leave the shared folder mounted on the reading room machines, since those are used for listening sessions, and don't sign out of the archive account on either one."}]
